Contemporary Issues: Tectonic Environments — a core area of A-Level Geography.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

mcqs.q: What are the four pillars of food security?
options: Walker circulation is the rotation of the Earth around the sun.
Food security means storing food for emergencies.
Availability (enough food exists), access (people can obtain it), utilisation (nutritional quality and absorption) and stability (consistent over time) — defined by the FAO.
Food security just means producing enough food.
The sequence of changes in a community of organisms over time, from pioneer species colonising bare ground to a stable climax community matched to local climate.
Succession means a forest growing taller each year.
Food security means storing food for emergencies.
Succession is just one species replacing another randomly.

mcqs.q: What is the Walker circulation and how does ENSO disrupt it?
options: El Nino is a current that flows from Peru to Australia.
Walker circulation is the rotation of the Earth around the sun.
Succession means a forest growing taller each year.
Walker circulation is the east-west tropical Pacific atmospheric loop: trade winds push warm water west, air rises in Indonesia, sinks over Peru. El Nino weakens it, La Nina strengthens it.
